We have a line in `process_final_updates`:
```python
state.randao_mixes[next_epoch % EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR] = get_randao_mix(state, current_epoch)
```

excerpts.content:
So options for transfers:
- status quo, with replay attack if you can fork eth1 to invalidate deposits, and insert your own
- replace receiver index with pubkey. Transfer signature easily checked
- special transfer object with pubkey of receiver is signed. But communicated with receiver index instead
- some mechanism to ensure a receiver index is bound to some initial deposit, to avoid replay. E.g. enforce transfer to come after block that has the initial deposit, or a more recent block.

excerpts.author: eth2_gitter_bot
excerpts.content:
<benjaminion> A (possibly dumb) question about the BLS test generators. Here, https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/test_generators/bls/main.py#L44 , there is the following comment and parameters:
```
PRIVKEYS = [
    # Curve order is 256 so private keys are 32 bytes at most.
    # Also not all integers is a valid private key, so using pre-generated keys
    hex_to_int('0x00000000000000000000000000000000263dbd792f5b1be47ed85f8938c0f29586af0d3ac7b977f21c278fe1462040e3'),
    hex_to_int('0x0000000000000000000000000000000047b8192d77bf871b62e87859d653922725724a5c031afeabc60bcef5ff665138'),
    hex_to_int('0x00000000000000000000000000000000328388aff0d4a5b7dc9205abd374e7e98f3cd9f3418edb4eafda5fb16473d216'),
]
```
Observations:
 - yes the curve order (for G1 and G2) is 256 bits, but the private keys are still members of FQ, so 381 bits.
 - this is why not all integers are valid private keys
 - so why are we using 32 byte numbers prepended with 16 zero bytes here? What have I missed?
 - when the test vectors are output to YAML, only 32 bytes are present for the secret keys
 - by putting back the 16 bytes of zero padding we are able to pass the signing tests fine - Milagro expects 48 byte secret keys (i.e. members of FQ)

Clearly, everything works as-is, but just wanted to verify that we have a common understanding that (deserialised) secret keys are 48 bytes long (not 32), in which case it would be better for the test vectors to reflect that.
